scope: Shared ChatGPT auth implementation and direct install/control/execution/native launcher integration only; not a whole-repository or deployment partition clean audit.
method: Read entire shared_auth.py/auth_storage_policy.py and current execution-mode change/recover; reviewed current native_main fixed UID admission and added file-store branches, manager status/verify/preflight, control capability guard callsites/update/rollback/recovery and stage_control capability publication.

Read focused test bodies for real file lifecycle, logout/refresh compensation, partial rename recovery, legacy backup, stopped-service barriers, no old-control downgrade and real UID launcher policy/argv. Other unchanged test bodies are execution evidence only, not a claim of full new semantic review.
Checked cached official 0.164 FileAuthStorage truncate/create0600/unlink implementation and provenance hash; no new network/credentials read.
Ran only local disposable synthetic compose_layers/check_file reproduction and post-fix require_file_store check. No full/remote test, live mutation or source edit in reviewed backend files.
semanticConclusions: First actual mode change prioritizes current mode including logged-out absence, quarantines the other login once, preserves separate home/config/history.

File moves retain latest content; compensation after startup failure transfers the current file/absence rather than restoring old credential bytes. Pending transaction and inode identity are checked before completing or reversing transfer.

Management lock, persistent start barriers and confirmed service shutdown precede transfer; ownership normalization is root control only. Ordinary launcher keeps fixed uid/gid/capability admission and gains no privilege.
Non-file auth configuration is refused explicitly before mutation receipt/service stop in execution preflight and before app/catalog dispatch in launcher. No keyring migration is attempted.

Control generations require sharedChatgptAuth=1 once retained shared state exists, including logged-out/pending state; old incompatible recovery is refused before service change with candidate recovery guidance.
System/status exposes safe ready/pending/backup metadata; arbitrary credential bytes never enter shared metadata or public summary.

preAuditFindings.trigger: Valid host TOML 1048504 bytes composes to a 1048813-byte generated layer under the existing 4MiB provider-layer budget. Original new auth guard imposed 1MiB on generated and namespace views.
preAuditFindings.impact: A valid existing configuration could fail app-server/catalog startup after upgrade or block mode transition.
preAuditFindings.resolution: Generated layer and bound namespace views now share provider_layers.LAYER_LIMIT; user/managed/project files remain 1MiB. Independent check accepts original compose output and still rejects non-file store and >4MiB.

latestPerFile.meaning: Deduplicated latest passing results for current test bytes, not a single full-suite run.

validation.independentVerification: Actual case IDs/counts and selected test file hashes verified. Run3:160pass1fixture-error; run4:60pass1fixture-error; run8:17pass. Latest per-file union162pass/0skip is not one all-green aggregate run. Run8 sourceHashes match all12 current reviewed files. Earlier reports retain explicit source differences.

limitations: Latest real Linux tests use isolated source/temp roots and synthetic file credentials. They do not perform OAuth network login/token refresh.
Real UID0/65534 native_main validates app-server/catalog argv and rejects auto store; final supervise is substituted, so not an actual Codex network/session test.
Service manager, health and idle IO are substituted in transaction tests; no live instance, nftables or service change.
The later operator-copy inconsistency and saved-proxy-enable UX observation belong to the separate upcoming deployment review/implementation, not this narrow auth approval.
